title: The Fogbank Tollkeeper
story: On the pearl-diving coast, Halvestrand the Grey Ledger rolls in as a wall of fog and refuses to lift until every diver pays a share of their pearls. The village divers pooled 640 pearls this season. Halvestrand demands three-eighths of the pool, then a second bite of 25% of whatever is left, and Mr 6 must know exactly what the village keeps before he agrees to anything.
question: How many pearls does the village have left after both of Halvestrand's demands?
solution: Halvestrand takes 3/8 of 640 = 240 pearls, leaving 640 - 240 = 400 pearls.
The second bite is 25% of 400 = 100 pearls, so 400 - 100 = 300 pearls remain.
praise: Taking the fraction first was spot on — the second toll just had to come out of what was LEFT, not out of the original pile.
hint: Find the pile that remains after the first demand, then take a quarter of that new number — not of the original 640.
victory: Mr 6 read the totals aloud so precisely that Halvestrand's own ledger caught fire from embarrassment, and the fog rolled out to sea muttering about audits.
imagePrompt: A little numeral-six knight standing on a misty pearl-diving pier holding a glowing tally slate while a vast grey fog-face with ledger lines for eyes recoils over the water at dawn.
